html:
SMTO-EXE-0151 — SMTO can't use the keyboard on that computer

GUID: 94243024-8754-5a9c-97cf-46f5a1b0f79c
Slug: ui-keyboard-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO wanted to press keys in an app, but keyboard control isn't available on that computer, for example because its Linux desktop uses Wayland. SMTO didn't press anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to fill in the field or press the button directly instead of using keyboard keys. SMTO can often do the same thing without the keyboard, and that still works here.
  2. On a Linux computer, sign out and sign back in choosing an Xorg (X11) desktop session instead of Wayland, then restart the Gateway. SMTO's keyboard control doesn't work on Wayland desktops.
  3. On a Mac, make sure the Gateway is switched on in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility, then restart the Gateway. macOS blocks programs from pressing keys until they are allowed, and the Gateway reports the change when it starts.
  4. In SMTO, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a new task. New tasks pick up the Gateway's updated keyboard ability.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows that Gateway as connected and a new task can press keys in the app, or SMTO completes the step without the keyboard.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the computer's operating system and the keys SMTO tried to press, to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't use other tools to get around the computer's input or privacy settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's UI component does not advertise keyboard input, has no keyboard backend, or could not map the requested key through its native keyboard backend.

What this means

  • The adapter did not advertise keyboard input, lacked a keyboard implementation or could not map the requested key through its native keyboard backend. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The adapter did not advertise keyboard input, lacked a keyboard implementation or could not map the requested key through its native keyboard backend.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect ui.status keyboard support and the exact supported key; Linux Wayland has no implemented input fallback here.

How to fix it

  • Check ui.status keyboard_input on the selected Gateway. On Linux, keyboard input requires an X11 session with the XTEST extension (Wayland has no input fallback); on macOS the host needs event-posting permission; otherwise use semantic actions such as ui.set_value or ui.invoke instead of key_press/type_text, and use only supported key names.
  • Use semantic actions or a native session with supported input. Wayland input fallback is not implemented.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use semantic actions or a native session with supported input. Wayland input fallback is not implemented.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported semantic action or permitted keyboard path performs the intended action on the exact focused target.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
